test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-II (Statistics) Official Paper-II (Held On: 19 Jan, 2025)
subject: general
question: If a large sample of size n is taken from a normal population with mean μ and standard deviation σ, the 95% confidence interval for the unknown parameter μ is:
solution:
The correct answer is: (bar x±1.96(sigma)/(sqrt n))

**Explanation:**

For a large sample drawn from a normal population with known standard deviation (σ), the sampling distribution of the sample mean bar{x} is normal with:

• Mean = mu 

• Standard error = dfrac{sigma}{sqrt{n}} 

At the 95% confidence level, the critical value from the standard normal distribution is 1.96.

Hence, the 95% confidence interval for the population mean mu is:

 bar{x} pm 1.96 ( dfrac{sigma}{sqrt{n}} ) 

**Why other options are incorrect:**

• Option (2): Uses bar{x}² , which is not valid for confidence intervals.

• Option (3): Incorrectly uses sigma² instead of sigma .

• Option (4): Uses dfrac{sigma²}{n} , which represents variance, not standard error.
